title: Firefighters
description: Control and extinguish fires or respond to emergency situations where life, property, or the environment is at risk. Duties may include fire prevention, emergency medical service, hazardous material response, search and rescue, and disaster assistance.

tasks.text: Create openings in buildings for ventilation or entrance, using axes, chisels, crowbars, electric saws, or core cutters.
Drive and operate fire fighting vehicles and equipment.
Position and climb ladders to gain access to upper levels of buildings, or to rescue individuals from burning structures.
Operate pumps connected to high-pressure hoses.
Participate in physical training activities to maintain a high level of physical fitness.
Protect property from water and smoke, using waterproof salvage covers, smoke ejectors, and deodorants.
Salvage property by removing broken glass, pumping out water, and ventilating buildings to remove smoke.
Take action to contain any hazardous chemicals that could catch fire, leak, or spill.
Extinguish flames and embers to suppress fires, using shovels or engine- or hand-driven water or chemical pumps.
Assess fires and situations and report conditions to superiors to receive instructions, using two-way radios.
Move toward the source of a fire, using knowledge of types of fires, construction design, building materials, and physical layout of properties.
Patrol burned areas after fires to locate and eliminate hot spots that may restart fires.
Orient self in relation to fire, using compass and map, and collect supplies and equipment dropped by parachute.
Rescue survivors from burning buildings, accident sites, and water hazards.
Respond to fire alarms and other calls for assistance, such as automobile and industrial accidents.
Administer first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation to injured persons or provide emergency medical care such as basic or advanced life support.
Search to locate fire survivors.
Participate in fire drills and demonstrations of fire fighting techniques.
Inform and educate the public on fire prevention.
Train new employees to control and suppress fires.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Maintain contact with fire dispatchers at all times to notify them of the need for additional firefighters and supplies, or to detail any difficulties encountered.
Collaborate with other firefighters as a member of a firefighting crew.
Dress with equipment such as fire-resistant clothing and breathing apparatus.
Inspect fire sites after flames have been extinguished to ensure that there is no further danger.
Select and attach hose nozzles, depending on fire type, and direct streams of water or chemicals onto fires.
Collaborate with police to respond to accidents, disasters, and arson investigation calls.
Prepare written reports that detail specifics of fire incidents.
Maintain knowledge of current firefighting practices by participating in drills and by attending seminars, conventions, and conferences.
Clean and maintain fire stations and fire fighting equipment and apparatus.
Inspect buildings for fire hazards and compliance with fire prevention ordinances, testing and checking smoke alarms and fire suppression equipment as necessary.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Equipment Selection
skills.def: Determining the kind of tools and equipment needed to do a job.

skills.name: Equipment Maintenance
skills.def: Performing routine maintenance on equipment and determining when and what kind of maintenance is needed.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Affiliated Computer Services ACS FIREHOUSE, Fire incident reporting systems, Microsoft Access.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.
